quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay on gaining knowledge from legends like Laila Ali
quotes.excerpt: I just love the fact that Laila was there and giving of her time to commit
quotes.quote: I just love the fact that Laila was there and giving of her time to commit to this cast and let us know the stories, give perspective. I know Amari Harwick had known the late Muhammad Ali and just to get the stories. I remember when I was an undergrad at Howard University, I looked across the yard one day and saw Muhammad Ali coming down the yard. I just felt surreal, and I am like, 'Yo, Champ!' And he just, at the time he had Parkinson's at that time, and I went over and was able to talk. Every person that I know that has ever met Muhammad Ali has an experience that feels like it is just bigger than life, and how gracious he was and charismatic. To get that by way of his wife pouring that in, that is part of the fabric of this production. That is the great thing about when you do have the estate's approval to tell the story.

quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay on the mental and physical toll of acting
quotes.excerpt: It was more than just the actor thing where, okay, I am going to do two a days
quotes.quote: My process is very similar, but with Sunny there was an expectation that I had for myself. I realized that there would be a pound of flesh to pay for playing this role. It was more than just the actor thing where, okay, I am going to do two a days, I am going to train, I am going to go on a calorie restriction, we are going to bulk up, I am going to learn the dialect of someone from St. Louis by way of Saint Joe, Arkansas. All of those things I got. That is what I have trained for. But what you are going to get is the soul. A man that has been through the things that I just said, you cannot just play at that. You cannot play at that. For me, it was going into the silence. It was carrying around like a 65-pound kettlebell throughout Toronto. That was like my ball and chain to represent the shame of being a champion and not respected, the lack of respect carrying that with me, a physical thing.

quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay on the pressures of being a professional athlete
quotes.excerpt: You got to deal with life, you got to deal with family, you got to deal with career
quotes.quote: That will drive you to drink, that will drive you to drugs, that will drive you out of your marriage, family fucked up. It is a fact. It is too much. You got to deal with life, you got to deal with family, you got to deal with career, you got to deal with decisions, and then being forced to do shit that you don't want to do.

quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay on his nine-month preparation for the role
quotes.excerpt: I had it at least about nine months with that kettlebell
quotes.quote: I was at least about nine months with that kettlebell. That was my friend. My castmates would see me with it everywhere, and they would be laughing and stuff because they are like, 'Here come Amon with the kettlebell.' It got to come to lunch with us. But I think people got used to me with it, and they understood that, you know, Sunny is carrying something different than young Cash.
